items.title: JEV AI: Fast Decisions, Confident Mistakes
items.summary: JEV is a specialized decision AI model: given evidence and a typed set of choices, it returns a probability distribution ... instead of generating an open-ended text answer. Three papers test what happens when that interface becomes a low-cost AI judge, an agent controller, and finally the subject of a semantic stress test. Confidence-based escalation can save expensive model calls, but selecting a valid action is different from generating its arguments; and a type-valid decision can still violate the supplied meaning of its label. The key question: when does a fast, confident decision actually mean what the agent thinks it means? All rights w authors: Type-Safe Is Not Error-Free: A Constrained Decision Head Follows the Option Name, Not the Rubric Bound to It Yu Sun* National University of Singapore sun.yu@u.nus.edu Junhao Xu* Fudan University junhaoxu23@m.fudan.edu.cn REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents Tiantong Wu Nanyang Technological University Singapore tiantong.wu@ntu.edu.sg Wei Yang Bryan Lim Nanyang Technological University Singapore bryan.limwy@ntu.edu.sg JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure Yubo Li Yidi Miao Ramayya Krishnan Rema Padman Carnegie Mellon University {yubol, yidim, rk2x, rpadman}@andrew.cmu.edu #airesearch #aitechnology #aiexplained

items.title: A Coding Agent That Runs a Podcast
items.summary: In episode 1029 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Katie Malone, Host of Linear Digressions about the AI tool she actually uses every week: the agent that produces her podcast. Katie explains that it is Claude Code underneath, kitted out with specialized MCP tools and instructions, so a coding agent that can already do tool calling, reasoning and planning becomes a podcast producer. She describes it as one of the tactical pieces of her burnout recovery, letting her relaunch the show without it turning into a huge time sink.
